s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with generalized weakness, weight loss, and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Renal involvement with proteinuria and leukopenia
key_facts: Six months of progressive generalized weakness
Noncompliant with hypertension medication for over three years
Dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the left lung base
Blood urea nitrogen 60 mg/dL, creatinine 1.69 mg/dL
Chest radiography showed bilateral pleural effusions
High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
Urinalysis showed pH 5, 16 WBCs and 27 RBCs per high-power field

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with generalized weakness, weight loss, and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Renal involvement with proteinuria and leukopenia
key_facts: Six months of progressive generalized weakness

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies, with low complement C3 levels, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Non-tender lymphadenopathy, bilateral pleural effusions, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Non-tender, rubbery lymphadenopathy and weight loss

shortlist.label: Wegener's Granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pleuritic chest pain, pleural effusions, and renal involvement

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute inflammatory arthritis of the elbows and knees

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including progressive generalized weakness, weight loss, dyspnea, mucosal pallor, lymphadenopathy, and pleural effusions, along with laboratory findings such as high titers of ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA, and anti-Smith antibodies, low complement C3 levels, and urinalysis showing proteinuria and hematuria, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). The presence of these specific autoantibodies and the combination of renal and pulmonary involvement strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can cause lymphadenopathy and pulmonary symptoms, the presence of specific autoantibodies and renal involvement are more characteristic of SLE.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The lack of malignancy found on CT scans and axillary lymph node biopsy makes lymphoma less likely.

rejected.label: Wegener's Granulomatosis
rejected.why: The absence of granulomatous inflammation and the presence of specific autoantibodies are not consistent with Wegener's Granulomatosis.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: While the patient developed acute inflammatory arthritis, the presence of specific autoantibodies and renal involvement are more characteristic of SLE than rheumatoid arthritis.
